label: VARYING_DOMAINS_RIGID_IDENTITY_AND_NECESSITY_4 transfer exceeds concrete NECESSARY_2: models
paraphrase: Closed controls over two universally accessible Bool worlds and Bool beings, with presence x = true or w = false. (1) abstractDrop: only being true is concrete; every actual concrete being is NECESSARY_2 at every world, while the forward transfer fails: in the countermodel, the instance at world false fails, because the non-concrete being false is present at world false and absent at world true (the Lean type certifies only that not every instance holds); and no actual concrete being is CONTINGENT_1 at any world, so the contingency node fails everywhere although the transfer fails. (2) concreteDrop: every being is concrete; every actual concrete being is NECESSARY_2 at world true, while the forward transfer fails: in the countermodel, the instance at world false fails (the Lean type certifies only that not every instance holds). So the transfer is strictly stronger than concrete necessitarianism, both in constraining non-concrete candidates and in constraining worlds other than the selected one, and its failure does not give the contingency node. Statements about these interpretations only.
